The suffix -iyy , called nisba () (the report) transforms a name into an adjective that indicates belonging. It is one of the most productive tools in Arabic: you will use it for nationality and languages, and then you will recognize it in hundreds of political, institutional and technical adjectives.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to form the male and female nyba from the names of the main countries;
2. say and ask for nationality, provenance and residence;
3. Grant the nysba as an adjective ( ⁧رَجُلٌ مِصْرِيٌّ، الطَّالِبَةُ المِصْرِيَّةُ⁩ );
4. appointing languages ( ⁧العَرَبِيَّةُ، الإِيطَالِيَّةُ⁩ …);
5. distinguish citizenship, ethnicity and language in presentations;
6. read educational charts and present people from different countries.

What to notice. Each nationality is an adjective in -iyy: ⁧لُبْنَانِيَّة⁩ , ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ , ⁧سُورِيَّة⁩ , ⁧إِيطَالِيّ⁩ . It agrees with the person: Laylā è ⁧لُبْنَانِيَّة⁩ , Khālid ⁧مُقِيمَة⁩ . ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ "resident" is the word of documents for "live" to...
The basic rule has three steps: remove the article, remove the termination -a / -ā / -iyā name, add ⁧ـِيّ⁩ (male) or ⁧ـِيَّة⁩ (female).

Because the termination falls. The nisba attaches itself to the root of the name: in ⁧سُورِيَا⁩ , ⁧إِيطَالِيَا⁩ , ⁧فَرَنْسَا⁩ the -iyā / -ā final is perceived as nonessential part and falls. In ⁧السُّعُودِيَّة⁩ the name of the country is already a female nyba (-[the kingdom] Saudi Arabia): removing the ⁧ة⁩ stays ⁧سُعُودِيّ⁩ . Not just countries. With plurals and other foreign names there are other exceptions: you will see them when they are needed. The pronunciation of -iyy. The nyba is an adjective like the others (A1-03, A1-04): follows the name and generally agrees and determination.

To say "Speak Arabic" it serves the verb ( ⁧أَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ⁩ , A1-14). For now: ⁧لُغَتِي⁩ My language is... ⁧أَنَا طَالِبٌ فِي صَفِّ العَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ I am a student in the Arabic course.
In documents, citizenship is ⁧الجِنْسِيَّة⁩ al-ǧinsiyya : ⁧الجِنْسِيَّةُ⁩ : . ⁧مِصْرِيَّةٌ⁩ It does not always coincide with the belonging of a person or his language:
• an Iraqi or Syrian citizen may be Arabic ( ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ ) or Kurdish ( ⁧كُرْدِيّ⁩ ), and have as first language Arabic or Kurdish;
• a Moroccan or Algerian citizen may be Arabic or Amazigh ( ⁧أَمَازِيغِيّ⁩ ), and speak Arabic, a language amazigh or both;
• ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ indicates membership of Arabic language and culture, not citizenship.

In professional communication, you use the term that the person uses for himself and, in documents, always distinguish the three data. Confounding them is one of the most common mistakes in journalistic descriptions.

The doubles of the nyba. Inside the sentence: ʿirāqiyyun min Baġdād , šurṭiyyun īṭāliyy(one) . Pause: ʿirāqī , īṭālī . To the female always -iyya . ⁧ع⁩ and ⁧ق⁩ in ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ . One ʿayn at the beginning and one qāf in the center: two sounds absent in English in the same word. Irāki with k is the Italian pronunciation to be avoided. ⁧ص⁩ in ⁧البَصْرَة⁩ , ⁧ح⁩ in ⁧حَلَب⁩ . Basra begins with the article and a ṣād Emphasis: al-Baṣra . Aleppo is ⁧حَلَب⁩ Ḥalab , ḥāʾ. Notes of use. The plural of the nysba in person is often regular (-iyyūn), but some have their own pluralities: ⁧مَغَارِبَة⁩ Moroccans (including Moroccans) ⁧عَرَب⁩ "Arabic" is equal to or greater than "Arabic"; ⁧أَكْرَاد⁩ "Kurdish." ⁧بَلَد⁩ means country, country, country, in Egypt and the Levant ⁧بَلَد⁩ It is also used for Christmas cities. ⁧مُقِيم⁩ is the word of documents: ⁧الإِقَامَة⁩ al-iqāma is the residence permit (s) or residence (s).
